**About the Role**
We are looking for an exceptional **Executive Assistant** to partner with our Northern Europe General Manager and Leadership Team.
This is a highly visible and influential role at the heart of our Northern Europe business. More than traditional executive support, you will act as a **trusted strategic partner**, helping our leaders operate effectively, stay focused on their priorities and deliver against key business objectives.
You will bring energy, judgement and exceptional proactivity – anticipating what is needed, connecting the dots and ensuring meetings, communications, events and executive priorities are planned and delivered to an outstanding standard.
If you thrive in a fast-paced international environment, enjoy creating structure from complexity and are passionate about making leaders and teams more effective, this could be a great opportunity for you.
**What’s in it for you?**
* Competitive salary plus profit share
* Pension and free private healthcare
* 4.5-day working week, giving you an early start to the weekend
* Flexible start and finish times
* Free on-site parking, Complimentary shuttle bus from local train stations
* Access to our recently updated on-site gym, including free fitness classes and a new Spin Studio
**What You’ll Do**
**Executive & Leadership Team Support**
* Own complex diary and schedule management for the Northern Europe General Manager, prioritising time against strategic and commercial priorities.
* Partner with the General Manager and Leadership Team to anticipate requirements, identify risks and remove barriers.
* Coordinate domestic and international travel, including flights, accommodation, transport, visas and detailed itineraries.
* Handle sensitive and confidential information with the highest level of discretion and professionalism.
**Leadership Meetings & Communications**
* Lead the planning and delivery of key leadership meetings, business reviews, town halls, planning sessions and off-site events.
* Shape agendas with meeting owners, ensuring objectives, decisions, pre-work and desired outcomes are clear.
* Coordinate and quality-check executive presentations, briefing materials, reports and communications, ensuring they are clear, compelling and delivered on time.
* Ensure meeting technology, logistics and materials are fully prepared and tested in advance.
* Capture key decisions, actions, owners and deadlines and proactively drive follow-through.
* Support the Leadership Team's annual operating rhythm, ensuring priorities and commitments remain visible and on track.
**Conferences & Major Business Events**
* Lead the end-to-end organisation and delivery of our Northern Europe Commercial Conference and other key business events.
* Coordinate venues, vendors and agencies, alongside budgets, logistics, technology, catering and the overall attendee experience.
* Drive readiness of presentations, agendas, speaker materials, communications and event content.
* Act as a central point of leadership during events, anticipating issues and ensuring a seamless and engaging experience.
**Operational Excellence**
* Build strong relationships across functions, countries and seniority levels, becoming a trusted point of contact for internal and external stakeholders.
* Identify opportunities to simplify processes and introduce smarter, more digital ways of working.
* Support wider Northern Europe operational priorities and onboarding activities where required.
* Create a welcoming, well-organized workplace where people can do their best work, while keeping the day-to-day office experience running smoothly.
* Keep the business moving by managing purchase orders and finances efficiently.
**What You’ll Bring**
You will be an experienced **Executive Assistant or Senior Executive Assistant** with a track record of supporting senior executives in a fast-paced, international organisation.
**You will also bring:**
* Exceptional organisation, planning and prioritisation skills, with the ability to manage multiple complex priorities.
* A highly proactive approach, anticipating needs, risks and opportunities before they arise.
* Strong business acumen and the ability to understand the bigger picture.
* Confidence to constructively challenge, influence and recommend solutions.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, particularly when working with senior stakeholders.
* Outstanding attention to detail combined with sound judgement.
* The ability to build trusted relationships and collaborate across functions, countries and levels.
* Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to remain calm and decisive under pressure.
* Experience developing and quality-checking senior-level presentations, briefing materials and communications.
* A high degree of discretion when handling confidential and sensitive information.
* The ability to work independently, take ownership and see priorities through to completion.
* Experience managing external vendors, venues or agencies and delivering large-scale events would be highly desirable.
**Digital & Technical Skills**
You will be highly confident using **Microsoft Office**, including Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel and PowerPoint, with particular strength in creating polished, executive-ready PowerPoint presentations.
You should also be comfortable with virtual and hybrid meeting technology, travel and expense systems, and project or event planning tools, with an enthusiasm for learning and introducing new technology that makes teams more effective.
**What Success Looks Like**
Success in this role means becoming a **trusted and credible partner** to the General Manager and Northern Europe Leadership Team.
You will help create an environment where leadership time is well prioritised, meetings and events are exceptionally prepared, decisions translate into action, communications are clear and compelling, and potential risks are identified early.
Above all, you will bring **proactivity, judgement, energy and a continuous-improvement mindset** – enabling our leaders and wider Northern Europe organisation to perform at their best.

**Job reference number:** SWT26/02
**Status:** Full time / Fixed term, until 31st March 2028
**Hours:** 35 hours per week
**Closing date for applications:** Wednesday 19th August, midnight
**Interviews will be held on:** Thursday 27th August
**The Role:**
The Stirlingshire Monitoring and Control Officer (MCO) will contribute to the protection of the Highland Line (HL), a coast-to-coast control zone which aims to prevent grey squirrels from moving north from Central Scotland into the red strongholds of the Highlands and Grampians. Progressed through a programme of targeted grey squirrel monitoring and control, you’ll help support the protection and expansion of red squirrel populations in accordance with the Saving Scotland’s Red Squirrels strategy. This role requires an approachable individual with experience in mammal control work that enjoys working outdoors and interacting with people.
**Main objectives:**
Delivering responsive and strategic grey squirrel control in the region primarily from the shores and islands of Loch Lomond, heading east to Callander and the Teith Valley to Doune; develop regional Rapid Response Monitoring networks in the region; recruit and train volunteers and external partners in grey squirrel control and monitoring; build relations with local landowners and stakeholders; and support the Argyll and West Dumbartonshire MCO with removal of grey squirrels from the Loch Lomond islands.
**This includes:**
* Carry out responsive and strategic grey squirrel control through trapping in priority areas
* Plan and support the development and expansion of a regional Rapid Response Monitoring (RRM) networks
* Assist with recruiting and provide appropriate training to volunteers and external partners in grey squirrel control, monitoring and detection methods
* Where required, carry out Operational Monitoring (OM) to assess squirrel presence e.g. feeder boxes and/or camera traps
* Monitor the spread of the squirrel pox virus through the Central Lowlands by carrying out trapping and testing in sampling survey squares
* Collect and maintain records on monitoring and trapping efforts using Excel, ArcGIS and the SSRS Hub (database) and contribute to reporting on project performance.
* Encourage interest in local red squirrel conservation with relevant local communities, landowners and stakeholders through media and events
* Support the Argyll and West Dumbartonshire MCO with the removal of grey squirrels from the Loch Lomond Islands through trapping and targeted shooting
**The successful candidate will ideally have:**
* A degree or equivalent qualification in ecology, countryside management or related discipline.
* A minimum two years’ experience in a relevant field, including practical wildlife management/ invasive non-native species control.
* Experience in collecting, maintaining and reporting standardised ecological data.
* Experience of working with landowners, gamekeepers, foresters and the public.
* Experience recruiting, training and supporting volunteers to undertake active conservation work.
* A good understanding of conservation principles, practices and legislation.
* Knowledge of native tree species and familiarity with the Trossachs and Stirlingshire area (advantageous).
* Willingness to occasionally work out of normal working hours.
* A full clean driving licence.
* Possess, or be willing and eligible to obtain, a Firearms licence.

# Staff Engineer for IT Automation & AI transformation (Remote)
Location London, Portugal Remote, United Kingdom Remote, Munich, Cologne, Dublin, Ireland Remote, Berlin, Frankfurt, Lisbon
Department Operations
Apply for this job
SoSafe has the ambition to become the leading human risk management provider in Europe. Our award-winning awareness platform triggers behavioural change by providing effective and engaging training and simulations on cybersecurity and data protection. Cybercrime is costing the world >$10 trillion annually and growing by 15% p.a. - we invite you to be part of the solution!
**Are you a visionary Staff Engineer**, excited about pushing the boundaries of automation and artificial intelligence deployed across a whole company? We're seeking an exceptional candidate to join our IT Engineering team to build the foundation for our AI-native future, in one of the industry's fastest growing SaaS scale-ups.
Things no-one seems to know yet:
* How to make traditional automation & productivity tools consistently useful across a whole business in a post-AI world
* How to balance traditional tools against foundation models and agentic working
* How to enable (and protect) citizen builders to use spec-driven design and self-built AI-agents to *actually* change the organisation, reliably, safely and at scale
We want you to solve these problems.
**Here's how you'll make a difference:**
* **Test-bed:** Architect,build and iteratea toolchain fusing traditional automation and productivity tools (n8n, google workspace, etc) with spec-driven design and agentic working, test out on IT and Security
* **Iterate:** Advocate, mentor and enableotherearly adopter teams to use our platforms, get value, provide feedback, iterate the platform
* **Standardise:** Build self-sustaining cultural practices across the organisation, enable whole departments, scale the platform for everyone
* **Drive the evolution of IT operations** towards an all-encompassing \**-as-code* infrastructure model through hands-on architecture and design
* **Contribute to the IT/Sec Operating System** as we move wholesale to build-not-buy teams
* **Mentor and level up** the existing IT engineering team, then whole departments, serving as a technical guide to accelerate skills transfer and foster a strong, ***collaborative*** engineering culture
* **Champion and** ***advocate for*** our shared automation and AI platforms and methodologies, driving cross-departmental adoption to break down operational silos.
**What makes you a great fit:**
* Demonstrated experience operating at a Staff Engineer level, ideally within an established, successful, cloud-native hypergrowth SaaS environment
* ***Hands-on builder and systems thinker*** - ***A background that includes*** hands-on coding, ideally in a platform or SRE team. IT experience is secondary, we need builders who can help others build better
* **A track record** of successful AI-native adoption, showcasing how you've successfully moved workflows beyond experimental prompts into robust, production-grade automated workflows or agents
* **Deep technical mastery** of at least some of: infrastructure-as-code, modern CI/CD systems (e.g., GitHub Actions) and enterprise-grade workflow orchestration (e.g., n8n, Zapier)
* **A pragmatic engineering mindset:** You understand that while agentic working is fast and flexible, it brings significant utilization costs; you know how to design hybrid architectures that balance speed with financial efficiency. When faced with a complex problem, you instinctively break it down
* **Great leadership, stakeholder management and communication skills:** The biggest challenge is always people, not technology. You treat internal teams as your customers and excel at explaining complex technical concepts to non-technical "citizen coders" and executive stakeholders alike.
**What you will get in return:**
* A mandate from the CEO to massively accelerate our AI-native transformation in every role, actually solving the AI-related questions that we’re all asking, at speed and scale
* A company comfortable with rapid change and iterative development - We love experiments that fail, as long as we learn from them
* ***Collaborative*** and highly supportive IT and Security team around you - We prize a safe and enjoyable working environment, good work-life balance and solid mental health above all other things
* Close relationships with super-smart, highly engaged peers across G&A, GTM and Product Engineering
**What we offer\***
* Work/Life balance: Flexible hours, 33 vacation days
* Wellbeing and financial support: Access to Open Up, corporate discounts
* Connection & community: Virtual events, collaborative team activities, and opportunities for local meet-ups
* And the list goes on: Tech equipment, referral bonuses, dog-friendly HQ
*\*Perks and benefits listed above are for full-time employees and may vary slightly by office location. These are just a sample — you'll learn more during the interview process.*

As one of the fastest-growing security awareness scale-ups worldwide, we leverage behavioural science and data-driven learning to empower people against cyber threats. Our Human Risk Management approach helps organisations turn their employees into their strongest line of defence.
Backed by leading VCs like Highland Europe and Global Founders Capital, we’re rapidly expanding across the globe. We’re looking for team players who want to drive meaningful change in cybersecurity, take ownership of their work, and grow with us.
If you thrive in a vibrant, purpose-driven environment that values innovation, diversity, and collaboration, then this is the place for you!

## Company Description
Source BioScience, comprised of Source LDPath and Source Genomics, provides industry-leading laboratory services in genomics, multiomics and healthcare diagnostics, partnering with biotechnology, pharmaceutical, healthcare and academia. For more information, please visit www.sourcebioscience.com.
## Job Description
The role has responsibility for the day-to-day management of the quality management system within Source BioScience, as well as supporting operation of quality across the healthcare sites within the business and will be critical for driving continual improvement across the company via feedback from the management system.
This role will support the Head of Diagnostics Development & Quality in the ongoing delivery of quality management, maintaining ISO 15189 and ISO 9001 accreditation, other relevant standards and ensuring regulatory compliance with CQC, MHRA, HTA and any other relevant regulators.
You will have a high level of responsibility to ensure the successful delivery of pathology services through effective management that meets the needs of users, in line with our company vision and quality objectives.
Source BioScience has locations in Nottingham, Cambridge and Chichester, providing diagnostic healthcare services (cellular pathology and molecular diagnostics) and genomics services to industry and academia. The position is based at the Orchard Place site in Nottingham. The role will require infrequent visits to other sites in the business as and when required (e.g., performing audits).
Duties include:
Day to day management of the quality system across the business and supporting implementation, consisting of:
* Performing audits of the management system, managing the audit schedule and making sure this is complete on time.
* Management of the eQMS system including: - Workflow module (incident reporting/CAPA). - Audit Module - Document module - Customer & Supplier modules - Asset modules - Administration
* Process improvement and incident & complaint management.
* Incident investigation and root cause analysis, including supporting other departments in the business to complete investigations appropriately, ensuring corrective and preventive actions are effective.
* Writing, and review of quality policies, SOPs and documents.
* Quality review and approval of documents across the business and ensuring appropriate document control is implemented.
* Ensuring the validation and verification policy is adhered to, ensuring there is a process in place for performing equipment, procedures, methods and software validations/verifications and maintaining in a validated state.
* Support the Clinical Risk Management process through integration into the management system and management of risk assessments and failure modes effects analysis.
* Preparing the Annual Management Review (AMR) and monthly quality reports.
* Produce monthly quality reports, reporting on KPIs and quality objectives.
* Supporting the business in achieving quality objectives – ensuring these are set, monitored and actioned.
* Co-ordinating the internal awareness of the needs and requirements of the users through the AMR, assessment and audit feedback, complaints, incidents and KPI/quality objectives.
* Provide training for staff undertaking quality related activities, as required. (e.g., training in performing audits and root cause investigation).
* Liaise with, lead and support accreditation and certification assessment visits and responses.
* Support any third-party audits by regulators or clients.
* Supporting quality leads within departments and at other sites within the business, with occasional travel if necessary (such as performing audits).
* Provide training for quality leads and any other staff undertaking quality related activities, as required.
* Deliver the expectation of the service users whilst also balancing the interests of the company.
* To lead by example, demonstrating professionalism to colleagues commensurate with post.
* To comply with safe working practises in accordance with Company safety policies
* To participate in the Annual Joint Staff Review process, in accordance with Company Policy.
* To perform any other duties as may be reasonably required commensurate with grade and experience.
* Attend any training endeavours as appropriate to the role or as reasonably requested by Line Manager.
## Qualifications
Minimum requirements:
* Experience of operating and being responsible for management systems within pathology laboratories to ISO 15189 standards.
* Minimum 3 years’ experience in either ISO 15189, ISO 9001 or ISO 17025 accredited environments.
* Auditing experience
* Experience and understanding of root cause analysis
* HCPC registered Biomedical Scientist status
Desirable:
* Qualification in quality management
* Experience of cellular pathology, molecular techniques, sequencing and genomics.
* Experience with GCP/clinical trials
* Familiarity with Q-Pulse
* Experience in risk management, ISO 27001 or DCB 0129/0160

## About the Role
As a Drinking Water Safety Plan (DWSP) Analyst, you will play a key role in ensuring South West Water maintains a proactive, evidence-based approach to identifying, assessing and mitigating risks to drinking water quality from catchment to consumer.
This is a varied and rewarding role that combines technical risk assessment, data analysis, regulatory compliance and stakeholder engagement. You will work closely with operational, scientific and engineering teams across the business to maintain and continuously improve our Drinking Water Safety Plans, ensuring they remain aligned with regulatory requirements, industry best practice and company standards.
Your work will directly support the protection of public health and help ensure the continued delivery of safe and reliable drinking water to our customers.
## Key Responsibilities
### Drinking Water Safety Planning
* Develop, maintain and review Drinking Water Safety Plans (DWSPs) in accordance with Regulations 27 and 28, Drinking Water Inspectorate (DWI) guidance and Pennon Group methodology.
* Support the identification, assessment and mitigation of risks to drinking water quality and sufficiency across the entire supply chain, including catchment, abstraction, treatment, storage, distribution and customer taps.
* Ensure hazards, hazardous events and control measures are accurately captured and maintained within the DWSP framework.
* Review and update DWSPs in response to operational changes, incidents, audit findings, emerging threats, new evidence and regulatory requirements.
* Work collaboratively across South West Water and the wider Pennon Group to gather technical information and operational data to support risk assessments.
* Ensure operational vulnerabilities, process control weaknesses and improvement actions are appropriately reflected within DWSP documentation.
* Maintain consistency, standardisation and alignment of DWSP information across the business.
### Risk Assessment and Assurance
* Analyse operational, compliance and investigative data to support evidence-based risk assessment and decision-making.
* Identify trends, failures, emerging risks and areas for improvement through data interpretation and analysis.
* Evaluate the effectiveness, resilience and verification status of control measures.
* Maintain clear and auditable evidence trails to support risk scoring and mitigation decisions.
* Support the DWSP Principal Scientist / Manager in risk prioritisation, escalation and assurance activities.
* Contribute to the continuous improvement of risk assessment methodologies, procedures and governance processes.
### Operational and Stakeholder Engagement
* Build effective working relationships with operational, engineering, scientific and regulatory stakeholders.
* Regularly engage with operational teams to verify the effectiveness of controls and process performance.
* Promote a strong culture of water quality risk management across the organisation.
* Coordinate and monitor actions arising from DWSP reviews, audits, investigations and assurance activities.
* Support knowledge sharing and best practice across departments and business units.
### Regulatory and Reporting Support
* Support the preparation of regulatory submissions, governance reports and assurance documentation.
* Maintain accurate and auditable records in line with company and regulatory requirements.
* Assist in the development and review of DWSP guidance, templates, procedures and training materials.
## Knowledge, Skills and Experience
### Essential
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to build collaborative relationships and influence stakeholders at all levels.
* Understanding of drinking water supply systems and water quality risk management principles.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving capability.
* Ability to interpret complex operational, scientific and technical information.
* Structured and evidence-based approach to risk assessment.
* Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
* Competent user of Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
* Full UK driving licence.
* Willingness to travel across the South West region and work independently where required.
### Desirable
* Experience within the water industry or another regulated utility environment.
* Understanding of Drinking Water Safety Planning principles, WHO Water Safety Plan guidance and Drinking Water Inspectorate expectations.
* Knowledge of Drinking Water (Water Quality) Regulations.
* Experience analysing operational, compliance or environmental monitoring data.
* Understanding of water treatment processes, distribution systems, pollution pathways or operational risk management.
* Experience using Power BI, GIS platforms or risk management systems.
* Knowledge of root cause analysis, audit processes or assurance activities.

**Position Summary**
We are seeking an experienced New Product Introduction (NPI) Engineer to support the transfer of new electronic products from concept and prototype through qualification, production release, and manufacturing ramp-up.
Combining electronic engineering knowledge with a strong manufacturing background, you will work across design, manufacturing, process, test, quality, and supply-chain teams to ensure products are robust, manufacturable, testable, and ready for repeatable production.
You will support products through the engineering design review gates, lead the manufacturing design reviews, and take ownership of production-readiness activities.
**Key Responsibilities**
* Support NPI activities from concept and prototype through qualification, production release, and manufacturing ramp-up.
* Represent manufacturing throughout product development, ensuring manufacturability, assembly, test, reliability, and production requirements are considered from an early stage.
* Support electronic engineering activities, including requirements capture, design reviews, component selection, verification, and validation.
* Support product design review gates and lead manufacturing design reviews and production-readiness reviews.
* Contribute to the development of manufacturing approaches, including process flow, assembly methods, tooling, equipment, inspection, and production-test requirements.
* Plan and support prototype, pilot, and pre-production builds, resolving design and manufacturing issues through structured root cause analysis.
* Support the preparation and release of manufacturing documentation, including bills of material, drawings, work instructions, process specifications, and test requirements.
* Work with suppliers and internal teams to ensure components, materials, processes, equipment, and resources are ready for production.
* Support the implementation of design changes and maintain configuration control of product and process documentation.
* Support the handover into production and assist early manufacturing activities until the required quality, yield, and process stability have been achieved.
**Required Qualifications & Experience**
* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electronic Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related discipline.
* Significant experience in electronic product development, NPI, manufacturing engineering, or product engineering within high-reliability, regulated, safety-critical, harsh-environment, or high-performance applications.
* Demonstrable experience transferring electronic products from concept or prototype through qualification, production release, and manufacturing ramp-up.
* Strong practical background in electronic manufacturing, including process development, assembly, inspection, production test, and manufacturing documentation.
* Good electronic engineering knowledge, with experience reviewing or developing schematics, layouts, component selections, and bills of material.
* Good understanding of design for manufacturability, design for assembly, design for test, and design for reliability, together with process validation, root cause analysis, engineering change control, and configuration management.
* Experience participating in cross-functional design and manufacturing reviews, with strong planning, communication, problem-solving, and hands-on production support skills.
**Desirable Experience**
* Experience with hybrid microelectronics, micro circuit modules, advanced electronic packaging, chip-and-wire, chip-and-bond wire, die attach, or wire bonding.
* Experience with RF, microwave, high-frequency, precision analogue, or harsh-environment electronics.
* Experience developing or manufacturing electronics for oil and gas, aerospace, defense, space, automotive, medical, or other high-reliability sectors.
* Experience with product qualification, environmental or reliability testing, process qualification, or manufacturing-readiness assessment.
* Knowledge of relevant IPC, aerospace, defense, or high-reliability electronics standards.
* Familiarity with process FMEA, control plans, APQP, PPAP, Lean, Six Sigma, or similar NPI and continuous-improvement approaches.
* Experience working with external suppliers, subcontract manufacturers, or specialist process providers.
**Other Requirements**
* You must be eligible for full security clearance.
* Occasional travel may be required for supplier, customer, or project engagement.

job_title: Software Engineer, iOS Core Product - Cambridge, United Kingdom
job_description:
The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
Over 50 million people use Speechify’s text-to-speech products to turn whatever they’re reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify’s text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its App of the Day.
Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.
Overview
With the growth of our iOS app, being the #18 productivity app in the App Store category and also our recent recognition as Apple's 2025 Design Award for inclusivity, we find the need for a Senior iOS Engineer to help us support the new user base as well as work on new and exciting projects to push our missing forward. This is a key role and ideal for someone who thinks strategically, enjoys fast-paced environments, passionate about making product decisions, and has experience building great user experiences that delight users.
We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount. Our interview process involves several technical interviews and we aim to complete them within 1 week. What You’ll Do
Opportunity to lead key engineering and product decisions
Actively shipping production code for the Speechify iOS app
Work within a dedicated product team
Participate in product discussions to shape the product roadmap
Maintain and enhance the existing complex app architecture
An Ideal Candidate Should Have
Experience. You've worked on products that scaled to a large user base
Track record. You have worked on various products from inception to decent traction. You have been responsible for engineering the product
Customer obsession. We expect every team member whose responsibilities directly impact customers to be constantly obsessed about providing the best possible experience
Product thinking. You make thoughtful decisions about the evolution of your product and support internal teams and designers into taking the right direction
Speed. You work quickly to generate ideas and know how to decide which things can ship now and what things need time
Focus. We’re a high-growth startup with a busy, remote team. You know how and when to engage or be heads down
Technical skills. Swift, SwiftUI
Technical Requirements:
Swift Programming Language
SwiftUI experience
Experience in Multithreading Programming
Working with CI/CD infrastructure
Experience with Fastlane
SOLID principles, the ability to write every single class according to SOLID
Experience with Git and understanding of different Git strategies
What We offer:
A fast-growing environment where you can help shape the company and product
An entrepreneurial crew that supports risk, intuition, and hustle
The opportunity to make a big impact in a transformative industry
A competitive salary, a collegiate atmosphere, and a commitment to building a great asynchronous culture
Work on a product that millions of people use and where daily feedback includes users sharing that they cried when they first found the product because it was so impactful on their lives
Support people with learning differences like Dyslexia, ADD, Low Vision, Concussions, Autism, and Second Language Learners, and give reading superpowers to professionals all over the world
Work in one of the fastest growing sectors of tech: Intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Audio

job_title: Senior Software Engineer, Windows/Desktop Applications - Nottingham, United Kingdom
job_description:
Mission
The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
Over 50 million people use Speechify’s text-to-speech products to turn whatever they’re reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. What You’ll Do
Lead the design, architecture, and development of native Windows desktop applications using Windows App SDK, WinUI (or related UI frameworks), C#, XAML, and — when needed — C++.
Define and enforce best-practices for Windows desktop development across the codebase: code architecture, performance, memory usage, responsive UI, cross-version compatibility (Windows 10/11+), and maintainability.
Drive accessibility efforts: integrate and validate support for accessibility APIs (e.g. Microsoft UI Automation or other relevant Windows accessibility frameworks), ensure UI controls, focus management, keyboard navigation, screen-reader support, and usability for users with disabilities.
Collaborate closely with product designers, UX researchers, QA, and other stakeholders to shape feature planning, UI/UX architecture, and long-term roadmap for the Windows platform.
Take ownership of full lifecycle of features: conception → design → implementation → testing → release → maintenance. Ensure quality, reliability, and consistency across releases.
Identify, diagnose, and resolve complex bugs, performance bottlenecks, memory leaks, rendering issues, or compatibility problems — and propose robust architectural or design solutions.
An ideal candidate should have
Required:
3+ in Windows desktop application development using Windows App SDK, WinUI (or similar), C#, XAML — and ideally additional experience with native Windows code (C++, Win32/WinRT/COM).
Deep understanding of Windows application architecture, including interop between managed code (.NET) and native code.
Proven track record of designing, building, and shipping production-quality desktop applications, with an emphasis on reliability, performance, scalability, and maintainability.
Strong experience with accessibility APIs on Windows (e.g. Microsoft UI Automation or similar), and a dedication to building accessible and inclusive software.
Excellent software engineering fundamentals: OOP, design patterns, data structures, algorithms, memory management, multi-threading or asynchronous programming (where relevant).
Experience leading technical design, mentoring other engineers, conducting code reviews, and making architecture-level decisions.
Strong communication skills; ability to articulate tradeoffs, collaborate with cross-functional teams, and drive consensus.
A user-centric mindset: focus on building polished, intuitive, and accessible experiences for end users.
Preferred / Bonus:
Experience with writing automated tests for UI — unit tests, integration tests, UI automation tests; familiarity with relevant testing frameworks.
Experience with performance optimization for desktop apps (memory usage, startup time, rendering performance, high-DPI support, responsiveness under load).
Experience with localization/globalization, right-to-left UI support, internationalization, accessibility for multiple regions.
Familiarity with telemetry, analytics, crash reporting, logging, and error monitoring in desktop applications.
Previous experience in shaping CI/CD workflows, release pipelines, and deployment strategies for desktop applications.
Demonstrated ability to take ownership of feature areas or modules and drive them long-term, including maintenance, refactoring, and technical debt management.
What we offer
A high-impact role: you will define architecture, shape the future of our Windows product, and directly influence what millions of users see and experience.
A collaborative, flat-structure engineering culture — you are not just a coder, but a builder and a decision-maker.
Opportunities to lead — mentor others, steer technical direction, and grow into broader technical leadership (e.g. Tech Lead, Architect).
Flexibility, autonomy, and responsibility: you define how to solve problems, own features end-to-end, and contribute to long-term product vision.

job_title: Software and Satellite Operations Quality Assurance Engineer
job_description:
We are seeking a skilled and motivated Software Quality Engineer to join our Mission Assurance team. This role sits at the intersection where software quality meets in-orbit operations, offering the opportunity to drive the operational performance of a satellite constellation. The role has two facets, you will own software quality assurance activities across the development lifecycle and also provide quality oversight to the team operating our constellation of satellites during commissioning, operations, and anomaly response. As the company implements its development roadmap, the distinction between these two aspects will blur with satellite operations increasingly transitioning to automated AI/ML tools to manage the fleet. The ideal candidate combines a rigorous, process-driven approach to software quality with an analytical mindset and operational awareness to allow them to ensure on-orbit anomalies are investigated and resolved effectively. This is a broad remit, so previous experience in both areas is not required. For example, a strong software QA background in a demanding industry (e.g. banking, medical, defence) will likely also have developed the analytical mindset needed to investigate on orbit issues. You will work closely with a fantastic team of software engineers, systems engineers, technical experts and spacecraft operators to ensure that our software and satellites are fit for purpose and that deviations from expected behaviour are understood, reported, assessed, and resolved with sound engineering judgment. What You’ll Do as Software & Satellite Operations Quality Engineer: Software Quality Assurance (Primary Focus): Define and maintain software QA processes, standards, and acceptance criteria for onboard and ground segment software across the full development lifecycle. Ensure that software verification and validation activities are comprehensive and correctly executed. Ensure the Software Development Lifecycle meets applicable quality requirements and standards. Where situations require deviation from defined process, ensure that this is performed safely and in a controlled manner. Raise, track, and manage non-conformances, ensuring corrective and preventive actions are identified and implemented effectively. Ensure risks are identified, evaluated and communicated effectively to the project and management team. Ensure that the software configuration baseline is maintained throughout development and mission lifetimes. Confirm all software releases are reviewed and compliant to standards. Contribute to process improvement initiatives and ensure compliance with applicable standards (e.g. ISO 29110, ECSS-Q-ST-80, ECSS-E-ST-40, or equivalent). Satellite Operations (SatOps) Anomaly Support: Provide Mission Assurance support to satellite operations, especially during critical mission phases such as Checkout and Commissioning, In-Orbit Verification and anomaly response. Lead and contribute to anomaly investigations, root cause analyses, and failure review boards, ensuring findings are well-documented and lessons are captured. Ensure the mission impact of anomalies is assessed and operational workarounds, corrective actions and recovery steps are appropriate. Identify links between incidents and coordinate response to common anomalies across the fleet. Ensure lessons learned are fed back to satellite development teams using non-conformance and corrective action processes. Liaise with software development, systems engineering and satellite operations teams to continually improve satellite operations tooling, improving Fault Detection, Isolation and Recovery (FDIR), increasing automation and raising the availability of the satellite fleet through transition to AI/ML based systems. Serve as the mission assurance interface to the operations team, software engineers, and systems engineers during anomaly investigations and resolution. Basic Qualifications: BSc or MEng in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline. 3+ years of experience in a software QA, systems engineering, or mission assurance role within a highly regulated industry (e.g. aerospace, defence, banking, medical). Proven track record of contributing to investigations and fault finding of complex systems. Familiarity with version control systems (e.g. Git) and issue tracking tools. Understanding of software development lifecycles (Agile and/or waterfall) and associated QA activities. Clear and concise communicator, able to present technical findings to diverse audiences including management and non-specialist stakeholders. Preferred Qualifications: Experience working with FMEA, FDIR, hazard analysis, or other dependability and safety analysis methods. Experience with satellite operations or ground segment software in an operational environment. Experience supporting LEOP, commissioning, or in-orbit validation activities. Proficiency in scripting or data analysis for telemetry analysis. Background in configuration management in a regulated engineering environment. Experience with failure review boards or anomaly resolution in an operational setting. Knowledge of relevant standards such as ISO 29110, ECSS-Q-ST-80, ECSS-E-ST-40, or DO-178C. Spire operates a hybrid work model, and this position will require you to work a minimum of three days per week in the office.
Access to US export-controlled software and/or technology may be required for this role. If needed, Spire will arrange the necessary licenses—this is not something candidates need to have before applying. #LI-MK1

The Codes Change Management Team is responsible for the detailed analysis, solution design and requirement specification for all Change Proposals in the Retail Energy Code (REC), Smart Energy Code (SEC) and Independent Gas Transporters’ (IGT) Unified Network Code (UNC) sectors. It is empowered and responsible for delivering changes to industry, proactively raising Change Proposals to address known issues and opportunities, and prioritising the change agenda to deliver an innovative, transparent and effective change process that focuses on consumer outcomes.
The Change Management Team are empowered and responsible for delivering a strategic programme of change to the industry, proactively raising Change Proposals to address known issues and opportunities and prioritising the change agenda to deliver an innovative, transparent and effective change process that focuses on consumer outcomes.
The Change Analyst will be responsible for the day-to-day operation of the change process through to implementation, developing solutions to address complex and/or technical issues and realise opportunities in the energy market. # Research Engineer
London (expect 5 days in office)Full-time
## About us
Telluvian is a London-based, VC-backed pre-seed startup. We use mechanistic interpretability, our understanding of what's happening inside neural networks, to make AI cheaper and more secure. Learn more at telluvian.ai.
## The role
We're looking for a generalist ML researcher to take on the interpretability questions we're facing and turn what we learn into things we can build. Prior interpretability experience isn't required, but more general experience with ML is.
Due to the nature of interpretability, this involves a lot of very open-ended work where there is no one right answer. In some cases you may be handed a research direction, but in many cases you will be able to decide on the direction yourself.
You'll need to be a competent engineer to do this research, but only in the ways that serve it. Confident Python is the bar; frontend skills aren't expected.
You'll join a team of fewer than ten people. Your research will form a key part of our product pipeline.
This is a full time position with flexible working hours. We ask that you're in person in the London office minimum four days a week.
Start date is flexible but our target date is early September.
## What you'll do
* Research interpretability questions, including choosing which ones are worth asking. You'll set your own directions as often as you're given them.
* Build prototypes from your findings. Often the end goal of a project is proving there's a tractable commercial use case for your research direction.
* Communicate clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, inside and outside the company.
* Collaborate with the rest of the team, picking up other people's directions quickly when it's useful to.
* Keep on top of published work, not easy in a field that moves faster than the literature.
## What we're looking for
* A computer science or related STEM degree, with relevant internships or prior work experience.
* A drive towards understanding pre-trained models. This is the attribute we weight most heavily.
* Competence with the Python ML stack: PyTorch and Transformers primarily. You need to be a good enough engineer to run your own research end to end.
* A strong work ethic with the ability to work in a self-directed manner. You will be working with advice rather than instruction.
* Confidence and good communication skills.
## Nice to have
* Production ML experience.
* Experience writing and managing custom kernels; JAX or CUDA.
* Prior interpretability work.
* A long-standing interest in machine learning and computational research.
* Commercial judgement to tell an interesting result from a useful one.
## What we offer
* Real ownership of research directions from early on.
* Meaningful equity in the company.
* Flexible working and genuine research freedom.
* 28 days paid annual leave.
* Workplace pension with employer contributions.
## How to apply
Send a CV and cover letter to careers@telluvian.ai. The process is an initial screening followed by two online interviews and an in-person paid work test.

* **IaC:** AWS CDK

* Experience with AWS and CI/CD pipelines

* Experience in early-stage or high-growth startups

# Social Media Editor
London, United Kingdom
**The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for.**
The New York Times is looking for a social media editor with experience in journalism, social media strategy, off-platform video promotion and collaborating on projects that involve crowdsourcing, social media reporting and research.
You will establish a vision for shaping and targeting our journalism for different platforms, and you will be responsible for understanding and developing new strategies, tools and workflows as those platforms evolve. This means you’ll be building our presence on Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, WhatsApp and emerging platforms. Engaging our readers, monitoring on-site and off-platform conversations for story ideas and integrating readers’ contributions into our report is essential.
You will know how to adjust social programming targets and priorities amid a shifting global, 24-hour news cycle and ever-changing platform landscape. You will also work with reporters and editors across the newsroom on how social media and readers’ voices can inform our journalism, both pre- and post-publication.
This is an in-office position based in London, and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.
**Main responsibilities:**
* Leading The Times’s social presence across our main accounts, ensuring coverage of breaking news and live events; conceiving and executing innovative social plans for enterprise projects; and leveraging videos, photography and graphics to elevate our off-platform report
* Support the increase in video production across the newsroom by prioritizing time-sensitive projects and ensuring that our video journalism reaches a wide audience off-platform
* Developing and refining the voice of The Times on all of our off-platform channels, exhibiting excellent news judgment and audience-sensitive framing
* Collaborating with Social Visuals editors and across our Video team, especially the video audience editor in London, on developing and executing visual storytelling formats and strategies for social platforms
* Building creative social native content (e.g., visual cards, Instagram stories, etc.)
* Skillfully editing, shaping and elevating headlines, copy and visual assets for social media
* Suggesting story ideas, identifying video opportunities and partnering with desks across the London newsroom to produce stories that:
+ Anticipate readers’ prospective social and search needs sparked by a Times exclusive or a news event
+ Respond to readers’ real-time social and search needs and trends
* Developing testing strategies around medium (images, video) and message (headline, social share text), to inform a constantly updating set of best practices for engaging off-platform audiences (Social, Search, etc.)
* Partner with editors across the newsroom to workshop on-platform framing of articles that leverage off-platform performance insights and reader interest
* Interpreting data and signals to know what pieces are the right fit for what audiences both on and off our platforms
* Tracking success through engagement rates, growth statistics, reader responses and other metrics, especially for video
* Working with journalists in the newsroom on best social media practices, including framing pieces for specific audiences
* Collaborate with other audience editors, in London and around the world, on flagging coverage opportunities informed by off-platform trends and sharing performance insights and case studies with desks
* Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
**Our ideal candidate:**
* Proven experience in social media and digital journalism
* Deep understanding of all mainstream and some emerging social channels
* Consistent record running Facebook, Twitter/X and Instagram accounts for major media outlets
* Demonstrated interest in visual storytelling, including through video
* Strong editorial judgment; comfortable with experimenting and refining strategies to optimize article-sharing for different social audiences
* A passion for news and a dedication to The Times and its journalistic mission
* Skill at bridging specialties, including reporting, editing, product, analytics, design and user research
* Strong writing and editing skills, and knowledge of Times style or the ability to absorb and apply it quickly
* Strong analytical skills and familiarity with how to use data to inform editorial decisions
* Experience working independently and collaborating across time zones

From pipelines to power plants, roadways to reservoirs, schoolyards to security solutions, clients look to TRC for breakthrough thinking backed by the innovative follow-through of an industry leader.
We recognize that the expertise of our staff is our strongest asset, so we generously reward employees for successful performance and invest in their careers through training and the development of new skills and certifications.
Overview
TRC is looking for an experienced consultant to join our Digital Grid Solutions team in EMEA, being part of the Energy Control Systems (ECS) practice. This role focuses on data management, data integration, network model management and MDM (master data management). The customer base will primarily focus on transmission and distribution system operators, and occasionally on data centres and generation.
Experience/affinity with CIM/CGMES, NMM, data interoperability and standardisation in control centre operations, substation automation, TSO-DSO integration, DER/RES integration and corporate asset management.
Responsibilities
Data management
Develop and implement data governance practices, including data ownership, data quality controls, validation rules, metadata, versioning, and lifecycle management.
Support data standardisation and harmonisation across network model datasets, systems, and stakeholders.

We are looking for an Analyst / Associate to own the data and commercial narrative behind the Group's West Africa (WAF) business. This is a commercial role for someone with an analytical mindset: you will build and maintain the evidence base — freight returns, cargo flows, and regional demand indicators — that lets the business make confident, defensible decisions about our WAF asset exposure, and you will be expected to use that evidence to influence colleagues, including pushing back constructively on the Chartering desk.
You will be the person in the room who can show, with data, that WAF-trading vessels continue to earn returns that hold up against the broader market, and that adding further WAF-exposed tonnage remains accretive to the Group even where it may tighten competitive dynamics in the trade.
• Regional data collection: build and maintain a live picture of the West Africa market — port and berth activity, cargo volumes, waiting times, discharge rates, and freight levels — using a mix of desk research, subscription data services, and on-the-ground contacts (agents, brokers, terminal operators).
• Demand-driver tracking: monitor and interpret activity at key WAF demand centres — notably the Dangote Refinery and Fertilizer complex, alongside other major industrial, cement, and commodity counterparties in the region — to anticipate shifts in cargo flows and vessel demand before they show up in the freight market.
• Returns analysis: produce and maintain the comparative economics of WAF-trading assets versus the wider market (comparable trades, benchmark indices, alternative deployment options), so performance claims are always backed by a current, defensible dataset.
• Investment case-building: assess the accretive value of adding further WAF-exposed tonnage to the fleet, including the trade-off between incremental returns and any dampening effect on trade-level competition, and present a clear recommendation.
• Commercial advocacy: represent the WAF data and analysis directly to the Chartering team, and push back — with evidence, not opinion — when chartering decisions or market assumptions don't reflect what the regional data is actually showing.
• Cross-team influence: work with Operations, Chartering, and other internal teams to get the regional data and updates you need, holding teams accountable for timely input even where you have no direct authority over them.
• Reporting and recommendations: brief the Head of Asset Management and the CEO on a regular cadence, translating regional intelligence into clear, decision-ready recommendations on WAF exposure.
• Relationship building: develop and maintain a personal network of contacts in West Africa (agents, charterers, terminal and refinery contacts, local market sources) as a standing source of ground-truth information.
What you'll bring
• A genuinely analytical mindset: comfortable building models and datasets from scratch, and equally comfortable defending your numbers in a commercial conversation.
• Strong Excel / data-handling skills; experience with shipping and market data sources (e.g. Clarksons, Kpler, Vortexa, MarineTraffic, S&P Global Commodity Insights, or equivalent) is a strong advantage.
• Confidence and communication skills to challenge more senior colleagues, particularly on the Chartering desk, in a constructive, evidence-led way.
• An interest in — or existing knowledge of — West African trade flows, ports, and industrial demand centres such as Dangote; prior exposure to the region (professional or personal) is a plus but not essential.
• Some grounding in shipping, chartering, or commodities markets, or a strong, fast-learning quantitative/commercial background (e.g. trading, research, consulting, or asset management) if coming from outside the industry.
• A degree in a numerate, business, or maritime-related discipline is preferred but not required if experience demonstrates equivalent analytical strength.
Why this role matters
West Africa is a strategic growth area for the business, and decisions about how much further to lean into it are being made now. This role sits at the centre of that decision: the person in it will directly shape how much confidence the business — up to and including the CEO — has in the numbers behind our WAF strategy.

## Description
The operations we automate run on work that has never been fully written down. There is usually a process document, and it usually describes the standard case. The parts that matter most sit with the people doing the work every day. That is why this work has resisted automation for so long, and why AI agents that can exercise judgement change what is possible.
As an AI Deployment Lead you own the deployment of our Virtual Agents end to end. You lead the customer through delivery, work out how their operation actually runs, agree what we are building and what we are not, and work alongside our Implementation Engineers to get it live and converted.
You are not a project coordinator. You are the person the customer trusts to understand their operation, and the person our engineers rely on to know what to build.
You'll join as our first AI Deployment Lead, working closely with product and engineering to build and mature the function, with an opportunity to step into a leadership role in future.
## Requirements
**About the role:**
* **Own deployments end to end.** Lead the engagement from kickoff through to a live, adopted automation. Set the plan, align stakeholders across operations, IT and the executive team, and hold everyone including the customer accountable to it
* **Discover how the work is really done.** Work alongside customer teams to understand the process as it exists rather than as it is documented: the volumes, the exceptions, the judgement calls, the decisions nobody wrote down. Turn that into a clear, agreed scope our engineers can build against and our customers recognise as their own. We're looking for people who are able to document the SOP, not only run the workshop
* **Advise on what to automate and what to leave.** Not every part of a process should be automated on day one. You make the trade-offs explicit, sequence what lands first, and make sure the customer understands what they're getting
* **Deliver alongside engineering.** Our Implementation Engineers own the technical design and build. You own the agreed customer outcome, scope and requirements, and you're close enough to the product to challenge a design, discuss access and integrations, and understand what's feasible
* **Define success and drive the decision.** Agree what good looks like and how it will be measured, capture the customer's baseline before we build, and lead the conversation that turns a pilot into a production service
* **Make the next deployment faster.** Turn what you learn into playbooks, patterns and product requirements. You're often the earliest signal on what our product needs to do next
**About you:**
* 5+ years in management, technology or transformation consulting, implementation or professional services, including time at AI Deployment Lead, Engagement Manager, Project Leader or equivalent level where you owned a programme end to end. We're looking for people who have run the engagement, not only staffed it
* Experience working inside complex operations and turning them into structure that technical teams can act on. Comfortable with processes that are messy, undocumented and internally contested
* Comfortable managing several deployments at once, with competing priorities and multiple stakeholder groups
* Technically fluent. You don't need to code, but you need to hold your own with engineers on integrations, access, data and feasibility
* Strong stakeholder presence. Comfortable with an operations team on Monday and an executive steering group on Tuesday, and able to build credibility quickly
* Comfortable handling objections and navigating organisational resistance. Automation changes how people work, and not everyone in the room wants it to succeed
* Highly analytical, ruthlessly organised and detail-oriented
* Highly autonomous and entrepreneurial, and comfortable in an environment where the playbook is still being written

* Big Four or MBB consulting background
* Experience implementing SaaS or AI products
* Intelligent automation or RPA delivery experience
* Experience working with customers in insurance, healthcare or another regulated operational environment
* Prior experience at a startup or high-growth company where you built process from scratch
*If you like being the person who walks into a complicated operation, works out what's really going on, and gets something live that changes how a team works, we'd like to hear from you.*

Deliver features end to end, including the Cloudflare Workers, APIs and integrations behind the interface.

Raise the technical bar for front-end craft, edge architecture and full-stack judgement across the web team.
Turn customer and business insight into better product decisions, not just completed tickets.

Turn design intent into polished, resilient interfaces, partnering closely with Product and Design.
Own responsive layouts, cross-browser compatibility and progressive enhancement across our brand portfolio.
Build accessibility (WCAG), Core Web Vitals, component quality and sensible front-end caching into everyday engineering decisions.
Full-stack and edge delivery

AI-first, quality-first engineering

Integrate work cleanly through Git, GitHub Actions and our Jira-based Agile workflow, contributing thoughtfully to planning, stand-ups and retrospectives.

Write clear, structured code and documentation that both people and AI agents can understand and work with.

Strong, idiomatic React and confidence across the modern JavaScript and TypeScript ecosystem.

Confidence extending into backend development through Cloudflare Workers or an equivalent edge or serverless platform, plus Node-based API services.
Practical, regular use of AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot or Cursor, with good judgement about when to trust, verify or reject their output.
Experience with a headless CMS such as Storyblok and third-party integrations, including forms and CRM or marketing platforms such as HubSpot.
A working understanding of accessibility, Core Web Vitals and caching across the browser, CDN and edge as everyday engineering concerns.
A habit of writing your own unit and component tests using Vitest, React Testing Library or similar, alongside effective collaboration with a dedicated quality function.
Confidence with Git, Agile delivery and CI/CD pipelines such as GitHub Actions.
Sound architectural judgement, clear communication and the confidence to shape technical direction without formal authority.
A proactive mindset: you investigate, ask why and propose better options rather than waiting for a ticket to define every next step.
Experience with internationalisation or localisation in front-end or edge applications.

A background in e-commerce or re-commerce platforms.

We’re looking for an experienced, hands-on **Senior Account Manager** to join our fast-growing scale up. This is a proactive, commercially minded role: you’ll own the relationship and renewal, identify and create expansion opportunities, and ensure customers realise (and can clearly evidence) the value Xelix delivers. You’ll partner closely with Sales, Product and Services to drive adoption, outcomes and long-term account growth.
**What you'll be doing**
* Own a portfolio of our highest-tier customers, acting as a trusted advisor and commercial lead across renewal and growth.
* Build and execute Customer Success Plans (CSPs) with clear outcomes, milestones, stakeholders and value hypotheses.
* Quantify, track and communicate value realisation (ROI/business impact), preparing and presenting success metrics and commercial narratives to executive sponsors and C-suite stakeholders.
* Develop a deep understanding of each customer’s priorities, operating model, systems landscape, and roadmap—using this to shape account strategy and unlock expansion.
* Run proactive account governance (e.g., EBRs/QBRs), ensuring adoption, stakeholder engagement and action plans stay on track.
* Monitor customer health and engagement to identify risk early, lead retention plans, and mobilise internal teams to protect and grow revenue.
* Identify, qualify and progress upsell/cross-sell opportunities, building business cases, aligning stakeholders, and partnering with AEs/founders where needed to close.
* Lead renewals end-to-end: timeline management, commercial negotiation support, stakeholder alignment, and forecasting accuracy.
* Triage technical and non-technical issues with urgency and strong judgement, coordinating the right internal resources while keeping customers informed and confident.
* Be the voice of the customer internally: capture product feedback, influence prioritisation with evidence, and manage expectations on deliverables and timelines.
* Stay close to market trends and competitive landscape, contributing to strategic initiatives that improve our commercial approach and customer outcomes.
**What you’ll bring**
* At least 3 years experience in Account Management / Customer Success in B2B SaaS (or a consultative commercial role), owning senior stakeholder relationships and outcomes across a portfolio.
* You have ample experience in managing complex enterprise customers, involving six-figure ACVs and engagement at senior levels.
* Demonstrable commercial track record: leading renewals, retaining revenue, and creating growth through upsell/cross-sell (with clear examples of how you sourced, shaped and progressed opportunities).
* Strong value-based selling and storytelling skills: you can quantify impact, build a business case, and present success metrics/ROI confidently to executive sponsors and C-suite.
* Experience running structured account governance (e.g., CSPs, QBRs/EBRs, exec sponsor plans), translating customer goals into measurable plans and driving them to completion.
* Comfortable managing complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise accounts—navigating economic buyers, decision-makers, champions and influence networks to drive change.
* Proficient in MEDDPICC or similar sales methodology

**The Firm**
XTX Markets is a leading algorithmic trading firm which uses state-of-the-art machine learning technology to produce price forecasts for over 53,000 financial instruments across equities, fixed income, currencies, commodities and crypto. We leverage the talent of the people who work here, modern computational techniques and state-of-the-art research infrastructure to analyse large data sets across markets quickly and efficiently, to maximize the effectiveness of our proprietary trading algorithms. We are actively seeking new methods and ideas. The models that drive our trading strategies have evolved considerably over the last 10 years, from econometric methods that gave our company its name, to trees, to neural networks, to modern deep learning architectures.
XTX Markets has an unrivalled level of computational resources in the trading industry, with a growing research cluster currently containing well over 25,000 GPUs with more than 1 exabyte of usable storage. Teams across the firm include world-class researchers, developers and technologists with backgrounds in pure math, programming, physics, computer science and machine learning. The firm is also constructing a large-scale data centre in Finland to future-proof its significant computational capabilities.
At XTX Markets technology is our business and we are a diverse organization which attracts outstanding talent from across all industry backgrounds. We are focused on teamwork and our people collaborate on all aspects of the business, working openly and with respect for each other, our clients and the market. The Information Security team at XTX Markets is accountable for all aspects of the firm’s IT security. From obtaining and transforming events and signals into actionable intelligence, to helping design and implement authentication and authorisation systems, and other security tools that underpin the XTX environment.
The team also assess third party security, as well as working diligently to keep XTX in compliance with a range of world-wide regulatory information security requirements.

This is a hands-on role. XTX prides itself on its ability to create and maintain software and systems that precisely meet our needs.

## Property and Supply Chain Risk Analyst
We’re looking for a proactive and highly organised Risk & Controls Reporting Analyst to support effective risk management, governance, and reporting across our Supply Chain and Property functions.
This role plays a key part in strengthening risk and control oversight, producing high quality management information, and supporting RCSA reporting. You’ll work closely with colleagues across Risk, ESG, Compliance, Procurement, Sustainability, and Property to ensure timely, accurate, and well governed delivery of key activities.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong analytical skills, an interest in risk and sustainability, and experience working in a regulated or complex operational environment.
## About the role
## Key Responsibilities
## Risk & Control Oversight
* Provide oversight and support for the effective operation of the Risk and Control Self Assessment (RCSA) process across Supply Chain and Property.
* Monitor and track risk events, control effectiveness, and remediation actions, ensuring these are accurately recorded, followed up, and escalated where required.
* Support the identification of emerging risks, helping to ensure timely awareness and escalation through established governance channels.
## Reporting & Management Information (MI)
* Produce accurate and timely risk, control, and performance reporting, including dashboards and insights for internal stakeholders and governance forums.
* Maintain and enhance risk and control data within relevant systems and trackers, supporting data integrity and audit readiness.
* Prepare clear, well structured management information packs for forums and committees to support effective decision making.
## Governance & Assurance
* Coordinate and support assurance activities, including internal reviews, audits, and control testing across Supply Chain and Property.
* Track and report on compliance with internal policies, regulatory expectations, and relevant third party risk frameworks, including horizon scanning activities.
* Maintain clear documentation and supporting evidence to ensure ongoing assurance, audit readiness, and regulatory reviews.
## Stakeholder Engagement
* Work closely with colleagues across Property, Risk, ESG, Compliance, and Supply Chain to ensure alignment and timely delivery of risk and reporting activities.
* Provide organised administrative and analytical support for governance forums, including paper preparation, action tracking, and follow up.
## About You
You’ll be comfortable working with data, engaging with multiple stakeholders, and managing competing priorities. You’ll bring a structured approach, attention to detail, and confidence in communicating risk and performance information clearly.
## Essential Skills & Experience
* Experience in risk management, controls, governance, reporting, or assurance within a corporate or regulated environment.
* Strong analytical skills with the ability to produce clear, accurate management information.
* Experience maintaining data quality across trackers, systems, or reporting tools.
* Good organisational skills, with the ability to track actions and meet deadlines.
* Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
## Desirable
* Experience supporting RCSA or similar risk frameworks.
* Familiarity with ESG or sustainability.
* Experience working with Supply Chain, Property, or third party risk management.
* Awareness of regulatory expectations and audit processes.
## About Our Benefits

* Our pension scheme (where you can get up to 11% from us)

## Description
### About Zego
Insurance hasn't changed much in over a century. The way we live, work and travel has.
Good drivers are the entire point of Zego. Seven in 10 drivers on the road are consistently good, but until telematics came along there was no way to prove it, so nearly everyone paid a price based on averages. Zego is the company built to change that.
At Zego, we're leading the AI evolution in insurance.
We move fast, without the layers that usually slow things down. AI takes the routine work off every team, from Finance to Product to Marketing, so people ship real code and launch custom dashboards in minutes. Engineering commits are entirely AI-assisted, which shifts the focus from team size to the quality of your thinking, and our data warehouse connects directly to an AI assistant for instant answers. Backed by a modern tech stack (Claude Code, Snowflake, Figma and Zapier) and a commitment to adopting new tools in days rather than quarters, you get complete ownership to do the most impactful work of your career.
### **Purpose of role**
Reporting to the Third party and Complex Claims Manager, the Claims Handler will manage their own portfolio of motor cases, focusing on claims exceeding £100k including losses for injury, credit hire, vehicle and property damage. This position requires not only excellent communication and negotiation skills but also a deep understanding of liability, indemnity, and quantum issues to effectively drive down claims costs while ensuring fair compensation for injured claimants. The role also involves handling large loss claims and acting as a technical referral point to provide coaching, mentoring, and training to the claims handling teams.
**What you will be doing**
* Manage a personal portfolio of complex and high-value motor cases, setting accurate reserves at inception and maintaining a clear claims strategy from first notification to resolution.
* Communicate effectively with customers, witnesses, insurers, repairers, solicitors, and medical agencies to expedite claim resolutions.
* Participate in strategic projects to keep the team at the forefront of industry trends and performance, and contribute portfolio insights to inform product and underwriting decisions.
* Investigate liability disputes thoroughly, gathering and assessing evidence including CCTV, dashcam footage, police reports, and witness statements to build a defensible position; manage Road Traffic Act obligations and Motor Insurers' Bureau (MIB) claims where applicable.
* Critically evaluate and challenge all heads of damage - general damages, special damages, care and assistance, loss of earnings, future losses, and rehabilitation costs, applying relevant case law.
* Scrutinise medical evidence from treating and expert witnesses, challenging speculative or inflated prognoses and instructing counter-experts where appropriate.
* Negotiate settlements directly with claimant solicitors and defendants, targeting outcomes that are fair, defensible, and below reserve.
* Challenge inflated credit hire claims using evidence of basic hire rates, need, and impecuniosity; make sound total loss and repair decisions aligned with market valuations and engineering assessments.
* Conduct structured file reviews and one-to-one coaching sessions with the broader claims team, contributing to training materials, technical guidance notes, and best practice documentation.
* Handle all claims in line with FCA Consumer Duty obligations, maintaining thorough file documentation, clear audit trails, and adherence to reserving protocols and authority levels at all times.
**What you will need to be successful**
* Proven experience handling all types of motor claims, specifically those in excess of £100k.
* Specific experience in Personal Injury and Credit Hire motor claims.
* Strong knowledge of indemnity and liability, familiar with Civil Procedure Rules, Serious Injury Guide, The Rehabilitation Code, and litigation procedures.
* A passion for a career in Large Loss, with a commitment to ongoing technical development.
* You work AI-first. You will use AI daily here, and we mean daily. You do not need to arrive an expert, but you do need to arrive curious, experiment fast, and take ownership of getting good quickly. People who wait to be trained will find this uncomfortable.
### What it's like to work at Zego
At Zego, we operate like a high-performing sports team. We come together as one, driven by ambition, backed by real support, and united by a shared mission to win.
Working here means having the backing, the coaching, and an inclusive community of Zegons across the UK and Europe who celebrate your wins and raise your game. It also means holding ourselves to high standards: moving with urgency, taking complete ownership, and embracing honest feedback that helps us continuously learn and evolve.
This is your opportunity for a career-defining experience, and one you will own.
.

Teams work better with time to collaborate and space to get things done. We call it Zego Hybrid: we gather in our central London or Halifax office weekly. It is about finding the balance between face time and focus that produces great work and a healthy life around it.
We also make a point of getting everyone in the same room. Teams come together every quarter, and once a year the whole company does, properly. It is a serious investment and consistently one of the best parts of the year...
### Benefits
* Market-competitive salary, benchmarked against your function and reviewed every year
* Annual performance bonus, linked to company performance and your contribution
* Share options, a real stake in the company and a share in the future you build
* Private medical insurance, for you and your family
* Pension, generous holiday, and £1,000 a year to spend on getting to the office or learning something new
* Cutting-edge systems and tools, so you always have what you need to drive your impact
If you're ready to help build the real-time, data-driven infrastructure for an intelligent world, we want to hear from you.

Strong B2B experience.
